name: Link
summary: Goes somewhere: another page, the provider's site or help. A link that opens in a new tab says so, so nobody's surprised.

when: To go to another page or site.
Inside running text, such as a hint that links to help.

whenNot.text: To do something on this page.
To go back a step inside Front Door.

anatomy.description: “(opens in a new tab)”, after the text, when it opens one.

props.name: newTab
props.description: Opens in a new tab, and adds “(opens in a new tab)” after the text. Use it only when leaving would lose someone's place.

states.name: Focus
states.description: A 2px focus ring around the text.

states.name: New tab
states.description: With the new tab hint after the text.

accessibility.name: Its text, including the new tab hint.
screenReader: Announced as a link, with its text.
A link that opens a new tab says so in its name, so screen reader users know before they press it.
notes: Underlined, so it doesn't rely on colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
Links inside running text are exempt from the 44px target size.

related.relationship: For doing something, not going somewhere.
A link to the provider's site, naming the provider.

guidelines: Say where it goes, such as “Manage your account on Bluesky”. Never “Click here” or “Learn more” alone.
Open a new tab only when leaving would lose someone's place, such as in the middle of signing in.

dosAndDonts.do: Say when a link opens a new tab.

evidence.point: Unexpected new tabs disorient people, especially screen reader users, who may not notice the change.
Link text that makes sense on its own helps people who browse a page by its links.
